notes:
This map blends two different pipelines on either side of the France-Spain border.

French side (Bayonne/Anglet/Biarritz/Hendaye area, ~102,900 modeled residents): same pipeline as our other scored France maps — INSEE Filosofi 2021 population grid (200m cells, total population) for residence placement (nothing to place, already fine-grained); jobs from INSEE MOBPRO 2021 real commune-to-commune commuting survey (place-of-work), spread across the destination commune's population-weighted Filosofi cells (no job-specific placement signal available); full commune-to-commune O/D matrix from MOBPRO.

Spanish side (Donostia-San Sebastián/Irun/Hondarribia area, Gipuzkoa, ~182,400 modeled residents): no equivalent to Filosofi/MOBPRO available. Real 2024 official population by commune (INE/Eustat) disaggregated onto OSM building footprints weighted by footprint area x floor count (building:levels, default 1). Jobs are NOT from any real employment count -- estimated as population x 0.42 (a regional employment ratio derived from Eustat/INE CAPV-wide statistics, not commune-specific), distributed between communes proportional to OSM economic-POI density, then onto buildings using the same floor-area weighting as residents. Commute flows within the Spanish side are fully synthetic (gravity-style distance-weighted assignment, 10km minimum-distance floor), not based on any real Eustat O/D table.

Cross-border flows (Hendaye/Urrugne/Saint-Jean-de-Luz <-> Irun/Gipuzkoa): real aggregate totals from the "Diagnostic sur l'Emploi Transfrontalier" (Eurorégion Nouvelle-Aquitaine-Euskadi-Navarre), sourced from INSEE 2013 / Eustat 2011 / INSS-CPAM 2016-2017 -- 3,212 south-to-north commuters (French residents working in Spain, concentrated 70% on Hendaye), 115 north-to-south (Spanish residents working in France, Gipuzkoa only). These are real measured totals the synthetic flows are forced to add up to, though the underlying source data is dated (~2013-2018, no more recent equivalent found) and coarse (a handful of commune-level totals, not a full matrix).

Dropdown answers above reflect the weaker Spanish-side pipeline since it covers the majority (64%) of this map's modeled population; the French side independently matches the quality of our other scored France maps (see e.g. Réunion, same Filosofi+MOBPRO pipeline). — Reviewer confirmation (2026-08-23): answers accepted exactly as filed — the author pre-applied the multi-nation conservative rule, classifying at the weaker Spanish-side pipeline (64% of modeled population; jobs = population × 0.42 regional ratio over OSM buildings, no Eustat O/D). The French side independently matches the réunion pipeline; the real-but-dated cross-border totals (3,212 / 115 commuters, 2013-2018 sources) bound the synthetic border flows but are too sparse to lift the O/D rung. FLOOR EXCEPTION applied as for guadeloupe: the FR floor is set by mainland Filosofi-grid maps; this is a majority-Spanish cross-border territory not previously covered, and no Filosofi/MOBPRO-equivalent exists for Gipuzkoa.
